canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across papers, the prevailing usage treats it as a model-level ability or capability: adapting at inference time to a new task, function, or query from a few demonstrations in the prompt, usually input-output or input-label pairs, without updating parameters. Many definitions phrase this as few-shot learning from exemplars, sometimes stressing that the model answers a novel query or new task purely from the context it is given. Smaller lines broaden the context to instructions, reference texts, unlabeled inputs, or general prefixes, while a minority use the term more behaviorally, as a prompting procedure or evaluation setup, or more formally, as task-level learnability.

Space of facets. Papers mostly use it as a broad umbrella, but they sometimes split it into model ability or capability, near-synonymous few-shot capability or adaptation, and multimodal extensions such as multi-modal long-context learning, where performance is improved by conditioning on many demonstrations. Narrower variants include selecting causal structure from context, and one formalization recasts the question as task learnability rather than model capacity; another mechanism-focused variant emphasizes exploiting statistical correlations inside the context. Explanatory papers also contrast it with learning in the weights and discuss it in meta-learning or retrieval terms, while some use the same label for the prompting procedure itself rather than the latent capacity behind it.

Space of measurement. Papers operationalize it with 35 linked measurement instruments and 30 linked behavioral indicators. The most frequent instruments are benchmark-style few-shot evaluations on GSM8K, MMLU, HellaSwag, MetaICL, and BIG-Bench Hard, with prompts often described in 5-shot or 8-shot form, while other behavioral operationalizations test few-shot performance on classification, reasoning, forecasting, associative recall, and multimodal tasks. These measures usually align with the dominant definition of learning from demonstrations without weight updates, though some broaden the test to long-context, multimodal, or general prompt-conditioning settings.

Links. Across 40 linked constructs, the recurrent claims are causal relationships from in-context learning to Generalization, Out-of-distribution generalization, and Reasoning, while related links often connect it to In-weights learning and Meta-learning. Papers also claim causal relationships from it to several downstream capabilities and task behaviors, and a smaller set reverses direction by claiming causal relationships from other abilities or training phenomena to in-context learning. Only a few papers report correlations, and the cited examples are specific benchmarks.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across papers, the prevailing usage treats it as a model-level ability or capability: adapting at inference time to a new task, function, or query from a few demonstrations in the prompt, usually input-output or input-label pairs, without updating parameters. Many definitions phrase this as few-shot learning from exemplars, sometimes stressing that the model answers a novel query or new task purely from the context it is given. Smaller lines broaden the context to instructions, reference texts, unlabeled inputs, or general prefixes, while a minority use the term more behaviorally, as a prompting procedure or evaluation setup, or more formally, as task-level learnability.

characterization_sections.label: Space of facets.
characterization_sections.text: Papers mostly use it as a broad umbrella, but they sometimes split it into model ability or capability, near-synonymous few-shot capability or adaptation, and multimodal extensions such as multi-modal long-context learning, where performance is improved by conditioning on many demonstrations. Narrower variants include selecting causal structure from context, and one formalization recasts the question as task learnability rather than model capacity; another mechanism-focused variant emphasizes exploiting statistical correlations inside the context. Explanatory papers also contrast it with learning in the weights and discuss it in meta-learning or retrieval terms, while some use the same label for the prompting procedure itself rather than the latent capacity behind it.

characterization_sections.label: Space of measurement.
characterization_sections.text: Papers operationalize it with 35 linked measurement instruments and 30 linked behavioral indicators. The most frequent instruments are benchmark-style few-shot evaluations on GSM8K, MMLU, HellaSwag, MetaICL, and BIG-Bench Hard, with prompts often described in 5-shot or 8-shot form, while other behavioral operationalizations test few-shot performance on classification, reasoning, forecasting, associative recall, and multimodal tasks. These measures usually align with the dominant definition of learning from demonstrations without weight updates, though some broaden the test to long-context, multimodal, or general prompt-conditioning settings.

characterization_sections.label: Links.
characterization_sections.text: Across 40 linked constructs, the recurrent claims are causal relationships from in-context learning to Generalization, Out-of-distribution generalization, and Reasoning, while related links often connect it to In-weights learning and Meta-learning. Papers also claim causal relationships from it to several downstream capabilities and task behaviors, and a smaller set reverses direction by claiming causal relationships from other abilities or training phenomena to in-context learning. Only a few papers report correlations, and the cited examples are specific benchmarks.

definition_agreement.reason: Most papers define in-context learning as a model or LLM's ability to learn, adapt to, or perform a new task at inference by conditioning on a few examples or demonstrations in the prompt or context, without updating parameters. A few papers broaden this to instructions, unlabeled or other contextual information, or refer to the prompting procedure itself, but the dominant use is still the same core phenomenon rather than a substantial competing definition.
